precepts.text: Because he hath sinned, and is guilty, he shall restore that which he took violently away, or the thing which he hath deceitfully gotten, or that about which he hath sworn falsely; he shall restore it in the principal, and shall add the fifth part more thereto, and give it unto him to whom it appertaineth. The recent matter was deceit: the fathers and leadership knew nothing until her sister discovered it, and they still were not going to say anything. You do not get the daughter and you still pay the fathers; that is why judgment goes forward, so no sister is beguiled by a brother claiming Exodus 22:16.
precepts.point: A sixth grader in the South stood up and put me on blast for a nasty note, and a sister in the world corrected an Israelite with a Bible in his hand, but grown women in the truth let men talk them out of their drawers and call it love.

note.label: The Vantage Point of the Elders: the Fathers Have Spoken

precepts.why:
Exodus 22:17: “If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins”. He has to pay, but he still is not getting the daughter. Somebody might say, he paid, so he gets to take her. Leviticus 6 shows the principle: “Then it shall be, because he hath sinned, and is guilty, that he shall restore that which he took violently away”.

Took violently away. To entice that daughter against her father's wishes is to violate him, and violation is violence. That is the same reason a man who steals an ox must “restore five oxen for an ox”: the owner was violated, and restitution is paid for the violent act against him.

“or the thing which he hath deceitfully gotten”. The recent matter was deceit. Her fathers didn't know anything about it, the leadership didn't know anything about it, nobody knew until her sister discovered it, and they still weren't going to say anything. How are you going to come up later saying, here's the law?

“Or all that about which he hath sworn falsely; he shall even restore it in the principal, and shall add the fifth part more thereto, and give it unto him to whom it appertaineth, in the day of his trespass offering”. The principal is the actual thing taken, and the fifth part is added on top. So you are not getting the daughter, and you still have to pay the fathers. That is why the judgment goes forward: we will not leave that kind of example for the rest of the sisters, to be beguiled by a wicked brother who says we're applying Exodus 22:16. That's a damn lie.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not steal; the trespass law enforces this commandment.
precepts.point: Stealing was not a sin unto death, but the Lord made the restitution heavy so you would never commit it again. It goes back to the commandment, thou shalt not steal, and to the civil law where an ox was restored fivefold and a sheep fourfold.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not steal.” The trespass law of Leviticus 6 enforces this commandment.

Lying to your neighbour about what was delivered you to keep, deceiving him, going into fellowship and not holding up your end, or finding what was lost and lying about it and swearing falsely is all counted by the Lord as a thing taken away by violence: he shall restore that which he took violently away. A Ponzi scheme or pyramid scheme sits right in that law.

precepts.text: Five oxen for an ox and four sheep for a sheep; the thief restored the principal many times over.
precepts.point: Stealing was not a sin unto death, but the Lord made the restitution heavy so you would never commit it again. It goes back to the commandment, thou shalt not steal, and to the civil law where an ox was restored fivefold and a sheep fourfold.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
The civil law made the thief restore many times over: “If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.”

That is the same principle as restoring it in the principal and adding the fifth part thereto: the value of what was taken had to be given back, with more added on top. A sorry would not settle it with the Lord; you could end up in debt for years over sticky fingers.

Stealing was not a sin unto death, but the Lord made the restitution heavy so you would never commit it again.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
“Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.” The whole book from Genesis to Revelation points to Christ, and the whole law of sacrifice points to him.

The ram without blemish, perfect as the Most High made it, is the offering without blemish that Christ is; the atonement the priest made before the Lord is the atonement Christ is; and who has become the high priest is Jesus the Christ. The sacrifice stood in your place for your sin, and he came in the volume of the book to do the same.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
Isaiah remembers “the great goodness toward the house of Israel, which he hath bestowed on them according to his mercies, and according to the multitude of his lovingkindnesses. For he said, Surely they are my people, children that will not lie: so he was their Saviour. In all their affliction he was afflicted, and the angel of his presence saved them: in his love and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bare them, and carried them all the days of old.”

“But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them.” Israel became the enemy of the Most High by sin. There are two kinds of enemies: the nations that are the natural enemies of the Most High, and Israel, who rebelled and vexed His holy spirit, and He was turned to be their enemy. That is why Israel needed a trespass offering and an atonement.

precepts.text: When we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, by whom we have now received the atonement.
precepts.point: The letters of Paul were written to Israelites living in those lands and called by their names, Romans and Corinthians, the same way we are called American or Jamaican today; written today they would be the letter to the Jamaicans or the letter to the Puerto Ricans.

precepts.why:
Paul writes that “if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.” The enemies here are Israel, turned into the Most High’s enemy by rebellion, and through the death of His Son the nation is reconciled, brought back together with its God.

And “we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.” The atonement the priest made with the ram before the Lord is now received by Christ.

The letters of Paul were written to Israelites living in those lands and called by their names, Romans and Corinthians, the same way we are called American or Jamaican today; written today they would be the letter to the Jamaicans or the letter to the Puerto Ricans.

The sin offering, meat offering, burnt offering, and peace offerings were prepared to make reconciliation for the house of Israel, and the trespass offering’s atonement in Leviticus 6 is the same work: bringing the nation that had become the Most High’s enemy back together with its God.

precepts.why:
“Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day.” That speaks of making food in your habitations, not the altar fire.

The burnt offering burned upon the altar all night unto the morning, and the fire of the altar was burning in it. The Levites were commanded to keep a fire burning on the altar continually, sabbath included, so the two commandments do not cross.

precepts.why:

“But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple. But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.” Israel leaned so heavily on the sacrifices instead of applying the commandments that they were confounded and could not see Christ as the Son of God when he came.

The priests were men, not women, and breeches are pants; they were made for the men. That is the linen breeches the priest put upon his flesh when he took up the ashes of the burnt offering.

precepts.text: They led him away to crucify him, and came unto a place called Golgotha; led away is the same as carried without the camp.

The ashes of the burnt offering were carried forth without the camp unto a clean place, and Christ fulfilled that figure: “after that they had mocked him, they took the robe off from him, and put his own raiment on him, and led him away to crucify him.”

“And when they were come unto a place called Golgotha, that is to say, a place of a skull”, there they crucified him, outside the city. Led away is the same as carried without the camp: the sacrifice was taken outside, and so was he.

“Let us go forth therefore unto him without the camp, bearing his reproach. For here have we no continuing city, but we seek one to come.” Put away the sacrifice as it was carried outside the temple, and come out unto Christ, bearing his reproach.

precepts.text: For we know that the law is spiritual; the statute for ever is understood in the spirit.
precepts.point: Christ told the disciples the Comforter would teach them all things and bring all things to their remembrance. Unless the Spirit of the Lord deals with you, you will never understand the Bible or the laws; that is why there was such contention between Christ and the Pharisees, for the Spirit had not revealed to them who he was.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
Paul writes, “we know that the law is spiritual: but I am carnal, sold under sin.” The meat offering, fine flour with oil and frankincense, a handful burnt for a sweet savour and the remainder eaten unleavened by Aaron and his sons, is a statute for ever in your generations, and a statute for ever is understood in the spirit.

To understand how a perpetual statute of sacrifice pointed to Christ, the Spirit of Christ had to dwell in you. Paul, who wrote that the law is spiritual, did not understand it himself until Christ touched him on the way to Damascus.

Christ told the disciples, “the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.”

Unless the Spirit of the Lord deals with you, you will never understand the Bible or the laws, this law of the meat offering included. That is why there was such contention between Christ and the Pharisees: the Spirit had not revealed to them who he was.

precepts.text: Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
The sin offering is most holy, and Christ was the sin offering, most holy. “Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps: Who did no sin, neither was guile found in his mouth”. Guile is deceit, and none was found in his mouth.

“Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously”. He left us an example that we should follow his steps; if you do not keep the commandments of God you are not following his steps.

precepts.text: If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father's commandments; that is how Christ walked.
precepts.point: The blood was not eaten: the sin offering whose blood was brought into the tabernacle to reconcile was not eaten but burnt in the fire. Israel does not mess with the blood; Esau eats the blood, not us.

note.label: Leviticus 6: The Trespass Offering and the Fire That Shall Never Go Out

precepts.why:
This is how Christ walked: “If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and abide in his love.”

He kept his Father’s commandments and abode in his love. That is the sinless walk that made him the most holy sin offering, and following his steps means keeping the commandments as he did.

precepts.text: The law of the sin offering: the priest that offereth it for sin shall eat it in the holy place.
precepts.point: Those were the instructions of the law of the sin offering: the priest that offereth it for sin shall eat it in the holy place, and all the males among the priests shall eat thereof; but no sin offering whereof any of the blood is brought into the tabernacle to reconcile withal shall be eaten, it shall be burnt in the fire.

note.label: Leviticus 10: Strange Fire and the Charge of the Priesthood

precepts.why:
Moses was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar because the goat of the sin offering was burnt when it should have been eaten. These were the instructions he was holding them to: “This is the law of the sin offering: In the place where the burnt offering is killed shall the sin offering be killed before the Lord: it is most holy.”

“The priest that offereth it for sin shall eat it: in the holy place shall it be eaten, in the court of the tabernacle of the congregation.” The Most High had given the sin offering to the priests “to bear the iniquity of the congregation, to make atonement for them before the Lord”, and eating it in the holy place was part of that work.

So when Moses asks, “Wherefore have ye not eaten the sin offering in the holy place, seeing it is most holy”, he is pointing them straight back to this law, “as I commanded.”

precepts.text: All the males among the priests shall eat thereof, but a sin offering whose blood is brought into the tabernacle is burnt, not eaten.
precepts.point: Those were the instructions of the law of the sin offering: the priest that offereth it for sin shall eat it in the holy place, and all the males among the priests shall eat thereof; but no sin offering whereof any of the blood is brought into the tabernacle to reconcile withal shall be eaten, it shall be burnt in the fire.

note.label: Leviticus 10: Strange Fire and the Charge of the Priesthood

precepts.why:
“All the males among the priests shall eat thereof: it is most holy.” The sin offering was food for the priests, eaten in the holy place, and that is what Eleazar and Ithamar should have done with the goat.

There is one exception: “no sin offering, whereof any of the blood is brought into the tabernacle of the congregation to reconcile withal in the holy place, shall be eaten: it shall be burnt in the fire.” When the blood goes into the tabernacle, the offering is burnt, not eaten.

That is exactly the point Moses makes: “Behold, the blood of it was not brought in within the holy place: ye should indeed have eaten it in the holy place, as I commanded.” The blood of this goat did not go in, so the exception did not apply, and the goat was to be eaten, not burnt.
